newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares hit highs ahead of EDP sale.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares hit highs ahead of EDP sale.

text.p: Portuguese shares hit highs shortly after opening on Monday on the eve of the admission to Lisbon bourse of shares in utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal.

"The New York stock exchange closed sharply higher on Friday when Lisbon bourse was closed for a public holiday, and tomorrow EDP will begin trade and will stimulate the market," said Diego Hernando of Lisbon broker Midas Corretora.

"The 30 percent of EDP's capital to be sold off in the privatisation represents about 15 percent of the capital of the whole Lisbon market, and if the stock rises 20 percent in one day (Tuesday), the whole market will rise," he added.
EDP shares will start trading on Tuesday following its partial privatisation. The share price and allocation will be fixed at a special session on Lisbon bourse after the market closes on Monday.

Nuno Thomaz of another Lisbon broker, Titulo Corretora, said optimism that agreement on how to move forward on monetary union would be reached at today's Amsterdam summit of European Union leaders was also supporting the Lisbon market.
The PSI20 index of 20 leading shares hit an all-time high of 7,267.49 points, nearly two percent above Thursday's close.
Since the start of the year the PSI20 index has risen by more than 41 percent.
Blue chip stocks Portugal Telecom, cement group Cimpor, Banco Comercial Portugues, pulp group Portucel Industrial and retailer Sonae hit all-time highs on Monday morning.
In the first hour of trade, some six billion escudos ($34 million) of shares changed hands on the official market.

Jose Freire of Espirito Santo Research said EDP shares could rise by between 20 and 25 percent on Tuesday as institutional investors who did not obtain all the shares they wanted in the privatisation sought to boost their holdings of the stock.
He said the BVL General Index, which includes all the shares on the bourse, could rise three percent on Tuesday on the back of the EDP sale.
The BVL30 index of 30 leading stocks rose 1.8 percent to 3,123.03 points after hitting an all-time high of 3,125.27.
Analysts expect the price in the EDP sale to be fixed on Monday near the upper limit of a range set by the cabinet of between 1,750 and 2,250 escudos per share.

Freire said he believed the main reason for the increase in Lisbon bourse on Monday was that the market was adjusting to the stronger prices on Wall Street at the end of last week while Portugal celebrated a public holiday.
